subject: Cybersecurity
title: Session Hijacking: Stealing Your Login Without a Password
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Session Hijacking: Stealing Your Login Without a Password.

hook.text: You logged in once and your browser remembers you. But that memory — a session token — can be stolen and used by others.

buildup.text: After login, websites issue session tokens (cookies) that prove you're authenticated. Whoever has the token IS you.

discovery.text: Session hijacking steals tokens via XSS attacks, packet sniffing, or malware. No password needed — the stolen token is enough.

twist.text: Infostealer malware exports all browser cookies in seconds. Attackers import them and are instantly logged into every account.

climax.text: Session tokens bypass all authentication. MFA, passwords, biometrics — none matter once the session is stolen.

punchline.text: Your session cookie is the master key. And malware can copy it in seconds.

quiz.question: Why does session hijacking bypass MFA?
options: Session tokens are issued after MFA verification, so stealing them skips all authentication
